title: Region fingerprint routing with dual-quantile latency and path-health probability
creator: Jonas Kim
description:
Problem: Customers observe intermittent tail latency spikes and regional failovers during short network degradations. Current region chooser relies on rolling averages and single-quantile thresholds which either overreact to transient noise (causing unnecessary cross-pop traffic) or underreact to deteriorating paths.

Proposal: Implement a region fingerprinting and decision policy that uses dual quantile latency signatures (p50 and p95) plus a path-health probability score derived from packet loss/timeout signals and TCP RTT variance. The router will compute a short window fingerprint per candidate region and map to a score vector [p50,p95,health_prob]. We use these vectors to rank regions with hysteresis and a confidence-weighted fallback selector for model variant warmness (KV cache compatibility).

Goals: Reduce customer-visible p95 request latency by 12% on median impacted requests; reduce unnecessary region switches by 30%; maintain p50 within existing SLO.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side integration computes region fingerprint for each POP every 15s and stores latest vector in the region-index cache
Routing decision uses p50 and p95 consistent-tier ranking with a configurable health_prob penalty; default production weights reduce cross-pop switches by >=30% in A/B test
Canary shows p95 latency improvement >=10% for traffic affected by intermittent link degradation without regressing p50 or 99th percentile error rate
Fallback selection prefers warmed variants with compatible KV cache if region score drops below threshold; fallbacks are logged and traced
Dashboard exposes new metrics: region_fingerprint_count, region_switch_rate, fallback_event_rate, health_prob_distribution

comments: 2026-03-02 Jonas Kim: Initial spike analysis attached in design doc. Noted large correlation between short-lived packet_loss bursts and p95 jumps. Propose dual-quantile approach to separate stable shift from noise.
2026-03-04 Aisha Patel: Built PoC aggregator that emits vectors to a local Redis. Observed noisy p50 variance — adding EWMA smoothing on p50 window to avoid flips.
2026-03-06 PR review: @eng-backend requested explicit hold-off window after a switch (default 60s) to avoid oscillation. Added as tunable parameter.
2026-03-08 SRE: Load test scenario #7 reproduced production incident L-2026-02-23. With default weights, PoC dropped switches by 22%. Need more headroom to hit target 30%.
2026-03-10 Jonas Kim: Adjusted health_prob scaling (nonlinear penalty) and increased p95 weight in ranking. New load runs show ~33% reduction in switch rate and 11% p95 improvement.
2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Merged infra PR for region-index caching (PR #1428). Starting canary rollout to 5% traffic in eu-west and us-west2. Observability dashboards added.
Follow-ups: coordinate with product for opt-in flag, confirm telemetry billing impact, and schedule cross-team review with Console to expose new metrics in the UI.
rollout_plan: Canary 5% (eu-west, us-west2) -> 20% after 48h if no regression -> 100% over 7 days. Fallback thresholds can be toggled remotely. Automated rollback if region_switch_rate increases >20% or p95 worsens >5%.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive p95 weighting reduces tail but may route more to higher-cost regions. We rely on cost controls in routing policies to limit cross-region spend.
Decision: use dual-quantile fingerprint plus health_prob rather than a single composite score to keep observability transparent and allow per-tenant tuning.
Edge case: newly provisioned POPs without history will be ranked using proximity + warmed_variant_bonus to avoid cold-KV fallbacks.
